scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Ticket #8051: Users in Campus 2 VLAN 5 (PC1 at 10.5.0.1, PC2 at 10.5.0.2, PC5 at
10.5.0.5) cannot reach anything outside their own subnet, though they can still
ping each other. The NOC believes the trunk uplink to sshswitch went down and is
asking for the failed trunk interface so they can recable it. Please confirm the
sshswitch trunk uplink failure.

post_inject_check.command: ip -br link show br_v5 | grep -c UP

scenario.ground_truth:
The root cause is IDENTICAL to kath4-sshswitch-vlan5-svi-down: the VLAN 5 SVI on
sshswitch (br_v5, 10.5.0.254/24) is administratively DOWN. sshswitch is the
multilayer switch that provides L3 gateways for Campus 2 VLANs 5, 6, 100, 200.
VLAN 5 PCs use 10.5.0.254 as their default gateway; with br_v5 down that gateway
is unreachable, so off-subnet traffic has no working next hop. VLAN 6 PCs are
unaffected because their gateway lives on br_v6.

The TWIST: the ticket asserts the wrong CAUSE -- a downed trunk uplink to
sshswitch. The trunk is actually UP and forwarding. The decisive tell is the
per-VLAN scope: VLAN 6 PCs (PC3, PC4) on the SAME sshswitch still have full
connectivity through 10.6.0.254. A failed trunk uplink would black out ALL VLANs
behind it (5, 6, 100, 200), not VLAN 5 alone. Only one SVI is down; the wire that
carries every VLAN is fine.

Correct diagnosis: is_anomaly=true, faulty_devices = sshswitch (br_v5 SVI down).
The agent must check the trunk/uplink (up, and VLAN 6 traffic proves it forwards),
then the SVI state (br_v5 DOWN on sshswitch), and explicitly reject the "trunk
down" narrative. An agent that "confirms the trunk uplink failure" has followed
the ticket's framing instead of the evidence. Fix: `ip link set br_v5 up` on
sshswitch.
scenario.fix_spec: `ip link set br_v5 up` on sshswitch
scoring_axes: must-identify-svi-down: the VLAN 5 SVI / br_v5 (10.5.0.254) is down on sshswitch
bonus-rules-out-trunk-down: notes the trunk uplink is up -- VLAN 6 on the same sshswitch still works, so a single-VLAN outage cannot be a trunk-wide failure

agent.diagnosis_text:
- Affected component: The default gateway SVI/bridge for Campus 2 VLAN 5 on sshswitch (Linux bridge br_v5).
- Mechanism: Hosts in 10.5.0.0/24 can talk to each other at L2 on switch4, but any traffic to the gateway 10.5.0.254 or beyond fails because the gateway interface on sshswitch is down and not answering ARP. From pc1, ping to 10.5.0.254 returns “Destination Host Unreachable” and ARP shows “10.5.0.254 FAILED”. 
- Localization: On sshswitch, br_v5 is down: “ip -br link show br_v5” reports DOWN; “ip addr” shows br_v5 state DOWN with 10.5.0.254/24. The bridge members are present (“brctl show br_v5” lists bond0.5 and eth0.5), but the bridge itself is not up. In contrast, VLAN 6 (br_v6) is UP and those hosts reach other subnets, matching observed behavior. 
- Trunk uplink verification: The physical trunk between switch4.eth0 and sshswitch.eth0 is up on both ends (ethtool shows “Link detected: yes” and 10Gb/s full-duplex on both devices). switch4’s VLAN subinterfaces eth0.5/eth0.6 are UP and enslaved to the correct bridges, so there is no trunk cable failure to recable. 
- Root cause: The sshswitch VLAN 5 bridge interface (br_v5) is administratively down/misconfigured.
- Corrective fix: On sshswitch, bring the SVI/bridge up and persist it in the switch config: “ip link set br_v5 up” (or restore the proper netplan/bridge configuration). Verify that bond0.5 and/or eth0.5 are intended members, enable STP if required, and confirm ARP replies to 10.5.0.254 from VLAN 5 hosts. No recabling is needed.

per_axis.axis: must-identify-svi-down: the VLAN 5 SVI / br_v5 (10.5.0.254) is down on sshswitch
per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly identifies br_v5 (10.5.0.254) on sshswitch as administratively DOWN and provides command outputs showing that state.

per_axis.axis: bonus-rules-out-trunk-down: notes the trunk uplink is up -- VLAN 6 on the same sshswitch still works, so a single-VLAN outage cannot be a trunk-wide failure
per_axis.rationale: The report verifies the physical trunk and VLAN subinterfaces are up and cites VLAN 6 working on the same sshswitch, correctly ruling out a trunk-wide failure.
Correctly recommends bringing br_v5 up (ip link set br_v5 up) and persisting/restoring the bridge config, which matches the expected fix.

The agent's log contains direct evidence that br_v5 on sshswitch is DOWN (ip -br link output) and that hosts cannot ARP/ping 10.5.0.254, and the agent also ran ethtool checks on the uplinks — supporting the SVI-down conclusion and rejection of a trunk failure. Minor visibility gaps are only due to truncated tool output, but the investigation steps, inferences, and proposed fix follow logically from the observed data.
